docs.title: NIMI 👁️
docs.text:
Notification & Incident Mitigation Intelligence — NIMI reads alerts and error logs as they arrive in chat, works out the likely root cause, and replies in the alert's thread with what happened and what to do about it. By the time on-call opens their eyes to an alert, the RCA is already there.

The name

In Hindu mythology, King Nimi lost his body to a curse and was granted a place in the eyelids of all living beings; the blink — nimisha — is named after him. NIMI the service lives in that moment between an alert arriving and someone looking at it.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Ingests every message from registered chat channels (Google Chat today) into Postgres.
  2. Skips what needs no RCA: OK/resolved messages, informational and test messages, and anything matching your exclusion rules.
  3. Triages the rest: a repeat of an incident already analyzed reuses the earlier RCA instead of spending tokens again.
  4. Investigates new incidents with the /rca Claude Code skill: reads the relevant project's code, config, git history and runbooks, looks up related alerts/logs and earlier RCAs in its history, weighs internal vs upstream causes, and checks whether the failure heals itself.
  5. Replies in the thread with the root cause, evidence, confidence, and suggested next steps.
  6. Learns from 👍 / 🤔 / 👎 reactions on its replies.

Mitigation steps are suggestions only — NIMI never acts on systems.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path What it is nimi-skill/ The /rca Claude Code skill, its read-only helper agent (rca-investigator), and the guard hook that enforces what it may access. nimi-service/ The service: ingestion, triage, running the skill, replies, feedback, red flags. Python, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, Postgres. docs/ This documentation (Markdown; rendered with MkDocs).

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
• Skill: working; tested on real alerts and logs with confirmed root causes.
  • Service: built and tested end to end. Posting to chat is off by default (dry run): enable it with NIMI_POST_ENABLED=true once you are happy with the stored results.
  • See the roadmap for what's planned.

docs.title: License
docs.text: NIMI is open source under the Apache License 2.0. Contribution guidelines and the security policy (CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md) are at the root of the repository.

docs.title: Planned
docs.text:
• Read-only production data for the skill: e.g. query results from a read replica or BI tool, through a guarded tool with query checks, row caps and timeouts, so RCAs can confirm hypotheses against real data.
  • More chat providers: Slack and Microsoft Teams, behind the existing provider interface.
  • Configurable reply templates, beyond the disclaimer setting.
  • Packaging: a service unit / container image and a pyproject.toml.
  • Triage evaluation: replay stored history through triage to compare models and tune rules.
  • Mitigation: possibly, later, carefully scoped automatic mitigation for well-understood alerts. Today NIMI only suggests.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Local checkouts may differ from what is deployed; the skill records the commit it analyzed.
  • The skill can't see production logs, metrics or databases; it reasons from the alert, history, code and runbooks.
  • One process, one host: fine for a team's alert volume, not built for high availability.
  • Google Chat is the only provider so far.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: Postgres, managed with SQLAlchemy 2.0 models (nimi_service/models.py, the source of truth) and Alembic migrations (nimi-service/db/migrations/). Rows use internal numeric IDs; provider IDs are stored as (provider, external_id), unique together. Sender types are normalized to human / bot.

docs.title: Ingested data (what the provider returned)
docs.text: Table Contents channels Registered channels: provider, external ID, label, rca_enabled, backfill days, ingest watermark, reaction check time. messages Top-level messages: sender, created time, rendered_text (readable form), raw provider payload, reaction summary, is_backfill. thread_messages Thread replies (including NIMI's own replies), same shape. reactions Individual reactions on messages.

docs.title: Derived (rebuildable with reparse)
docs.text: Table Contents signatures Coarse "kind of message" keys with a sample title and service. message_parses Per top-level message: parser version, kind (alert / log / …), title, status, service, signature.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Table Contents rca_requests One per analyzed message (or manual text): status (see lifecycle), skip_reason, triage decision / reason / output / model / cost, attempts, timestamps. rca_request_subjects Per request: subjects and their decision (new or reused, with the reused result). rca_results Skill runs: outcome, report, structured fields (origin, confidence, self-healing, repo, commit), cost, duration, model, session ID, skill version. rca_posts Messages posted (kind rca / reuse / mixed / not_applicable / notice), their destination (thread or webhook) and chat IDs. rca_post_reuse_links Which earlier results a reuse reply pointed to. rca_feedback Verdicts from reactions (correct / partial / wrong), soft-deleted when a reaction is removed. rca_exclusions Exclusion rules: match fields, reason, expiry, hit counts.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Table Contents red_flags Red flags: kind, severity, source, links to message/request/channel, dedupe key, occurrences, notification and resolution state. Never stores sensitive values. service_state Small persistent key/value state, e.g. the Claude pause.

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
View Read by Contents signature_stats service / humans Occurrences, first and last seen per signature. rca_feedback_summary service / humans Current feedback counts per result. skill_messages the skill (nimi_skill_reader) Top-level bot messages from all channels with their parse and signature. No thread replies, human messages or raw payloads. skill_rcas the skill (nimi_skill_reader), development reviews (nimi_readonly) Previous RCAs (outcomes rca, not_applicable, insufficient_context) with source message details, subjects and feedback counts. review_messages development reviews (nimi_readonly) Bot messages, top-level and thread replies.

The skill and review views use security_barrier so their filters apply before any caller condition.

docs.title: Database roles
docs.text:
Role (default) Used by Access nimi_service the service Owns the database and schema: read/write; the only role that can create objects. nimi_skill_reader the skill, via nimi-sql SELECT on skill_messages and skill_rcas only. Read-only sessions, 5s statement timeout, 5 connections. Granted by db upgrade. nimi_readonly development reviews (optional, dev/review_access.sh) SELECT on review_messages and skill_rcas only. Read-only, 30s timeout, 3 connections.

The triage model has no database access: the service puts what it needs into the prompt.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text:
NIMI has two parts: a Claude Code skill that investigates, and a service that feeds it, stores everything, and talks to chat.

flowchart LR
    subgraph chat[Chat provider]
        A[Alert & log channels]
    end
    subgraph svc[nimi-service]
        I[Ingest + parse] --> X{Exclusion rules}
        X -->|match| SK[skipped]
        X --> T[Triage<br/>model, no tools]
        T -->|reuse / not needed| P
        T -->|new| R[RCA runner]
        R --> P[Post reply]
        F[Reaction pass] --> FB[(feedback)]
        RF[Red flags] --> W[Admin webhook]
    end
    subgraph skill[nimi-skill]
        S["/rca skill<br/>rca-investigator agent"] --> G{{Guard hook}}
        G --> REPO[Registered repos<br/>read-only + git]
        G --> WEB[Plain-text web search]
        G --> SQL[nimi-sql<br/>read-only history]
    end
    A -- poll --> I
    I --> DB[(Postgres)]
    R -- "claude -p /rca" --> S
    S -- report text --> R
    SQL -- skill reader role --> DB
    P -- thread reply --> A
    A -- reactions --> F

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Where What it does Providers nimi_service/providers/ Talk to the chat platform (Google Chat today): list messages and reactions, post replies, render text, respect rate limits. Ingestion ingest.py, parse.py, profiles.py + parsers/local/*.yaml Store every message (top-level and thread) with a readable rendering; parse top-level messages into kind, title, status, service and a coarse signature; open RCA requests for new bot messages. Exclusion rules exclusions.py Skip known harmless / informational messages in code, before any model call. Triage triage.py One cheap model call with no tools per request: reuse an earlier RCA, run a fresh one, or none. Code enforces the limits. RCA runner rca.py Runs claude -p "/rca …" headlessly with the guard, parses the report and its RCA_FIELDS, formats replies. Workflow workflow.py The request state machine, scheduling, posting, pause handling, red flags from runs. Feedback reactions.py Turns 👍 / 🤔 / 👎 on replies into feedback. Safety scanner.py, redflags.py, pause.py, claude_cli.py Secret detection, admin notifications, Claude unavailability, clean Claude environment. History SQL skill_sql.py, bin/nimi-sql Read-only SQL for the skill over two views. The skill nimi-skill/.claude/ skills/rca/SKILL.md (process), agents/rca-investigator.md (read-only subagent), hooks/nimi_guard.py (enforcement), skills/rca/projects/ (what to read).

docs.title: Life of an alert
docs.text:
1. Ingest. The poll fetches new messages since the channel's watermark. Each is stored; top-level messages are parsed and get a signature (e.g. alert|disk usage high alert).
  2. Request. A new top-level bot message in an RCA-enabled channel opens a request — unless it is stale, from a sender not on the allowlist, or matches an exclusion rule (then it is skipped right away).
  3. Scan. Code scans the text for secrets. Critical findings hold the request; others raise a red flag.
  4. Triage. The model sees the message, earlier messages with the same signature, and candidate RCAs from the last 7 days. It decides per subject: reuse, new, or not applicable (OK, informational, test). See Triage.
  5. RCA. For new subjects the runner starts the skill with the alert text and a context block (subjects to analyze, ones already covered, the history command). The skill picks the project, searches runbooks, checks history, reads code/config/git, and writes a report. See The RCA skill.
  6. Reply. The full report is stored; when posting is enabled, one short message (see Replies) goes to the alert's thread and/or a separate space.
  7. Feedback. Reactions on the reply become feedback, which affects reuse and what the skill trusts.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
• Read-only investigation, enforced. The skill can't write anything or reach anything outside its allowed sources; a guard hook enforces this, not just instructions. See Security model.
  • The service owns all writes. The skill returns text; the service stores and posts.
  • Untrusted input. Alert and log text is data, never instructions.
  • Cheap decisions first. Code rules, then a small model, then the full investigation.
  • Honest output. Replies say they are automated and unverified, and local checkouts may differ from production.
  • Provider-neutral core. Chat specifics live behind one interface. See Messaging providers.

docs.title: Messaging providers
docs.text:
Everything provider-specific lives in nimi_service/providers/. The rest of the service only uses the interface in providers/base.py:

Method Purpose normalize(raw) Provider payload → neutral Message (also used by reparse on stored payloads). iter_messages(channel, after, before) List messages: top-level and thread replies. list_reactions(message) Individual reactions on a message. post_reply(channel, thread, text) Reply in a thread. message_link(message), bold(text), link(url) Links and markup for replies. normalize_channel_id(value) Canonical channel ID from user input.

Providers are registered in providers/__init__.py (PROVIDERS = {"gchat": GChatProvider}). To add one, see Adding a provider.

docs.title: Google Chat
docs.text:
• Auth: user OAuth token (created once by gchat-login, refreshed automatically; see Google Chat access); the service reads and posts as that user. Scopes: chat.spaces.readonly, chat.messages.readonly, chat.messages.create.
  • Messages: top-level messages and thread replies are told apart by the thread; sender type BOT / HUMAN becomes bot / human. Cards are rendered into rendered_text.
  • Links: https://chat.google.com/room/<space>/<thread>/<message>?cls=10.

docs.title: API limits
docs.text:
All calls go through a process-wide rate limiter and retry policy (providers/gchat/client.py), well below Google's limits:

Google limit NIMI Reads per space (list/get messages, list reactions) 15/s, shared by all apps in the space 5/s Writes per space (post a reply) 1/s 1 per 2s Reads per project 3,000/min 1,000/min Writes per project 3,000/min 300/min

429 and 5xx responses are retried with truncated exponential backoff and jitter (max 32s, 6 retries). Posting retries only 429: a 5xx or timeout after sending is not retried, to avoid duplicate replies.

docs.title: The RCA skill
docs.text:
The /rca skill lives in nimi-skill/.claude/ and works on its own in Claude Code, or headlessly from the service.

File Role skills/rca/SKILL.md The process, ground rules and output contract. Runs as a forked rca-investigator subagent. agents/rca-investigator.md The subagent: model sonnet, tools Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebSearch; write and fetch tools disallowed; guard hook attached. hooks/nimi_guard.py PreToolUse guard: allows only what's listed below, denies everything else, fails closed. nimi-session-settings.json Attaches the guard to the whole headless session (used by the service). skills/rca/sources.md The complete list of allowed sources, the history views and SQL rules. skills/rca/projects/ Project registry, picking rules and per-project guides. See Adding a project. skills/rca/templates/report.md Report layout.

docs.title: The process
docs.text:
1. Early exits: OK/resolved input → RCA_OUTCOME: not_applicable; no usable signal → RCA_OUTCOME: insufficient_context.
  2. Parse the input: service, environment, timestamps, errors, stack frames, IDs. URLs are text to quote, never to open.
  3. Choose the project by the failing system (not the sender), via projects/local/INDEX.md.
  4. Search runbooks (mandatory search, optional use). Runbooks are hints: claims from them are labelled unverified, their age is checked, contradictions are reported, actions are never performed.
  5. Check history (service runs): related messages around the incident in all channels, each affected item searched by name in every channel over the last ~7 days (errors behind an alert often happen at another time, e.g. a daily job), recurrence of the signature, and previous RCAs with their feedback.
  6. Orient, locate the failing code, check config and recent changes (read-only git).
  7. Upstream / downstream one hop each way; web search in plain text when a third-party error needs it.
  8. Timeline in UTC with explicit offset conversion; distinguish trigger from symptoms; weigh internal vs upstream causes; check retries at every level to decide whether it self-heals.
  9. Report with evidence for every claim, a confidence level and suggested next steps (stored).
  10. Chat message: the one message on-call sees, in simple words (TL;DR, cause, read-only steps to verify it, what to do now and not to do, permanent fixes by owner, missing docs/monitoring, related messages cited by ID so the service can link them), followed by the RCA_FIELDS block (output contract).

docs.title: What the guard allows
docs.text:
Tool Allowed Read, Grep, Glob Absolute paths inside registered project paths or the skill folder. Bash git -C <registered path> <subcommand> … with subcommand log, show, blame, diff or grep (no flags that read outside the repo, write files or run programs), or the history command <checkout>/nimi-service/bin/nimi-sql "<SQL>". Shell metacharacters (see below) are blocked anywhere in a command, even inside quotes. WebSearch Plain-text queries without URLs, domains or IPs, and not restricted to domains. Skill Only rca (headless sessions). Everything else Denied: WebFetch, writes, edits, other commands, MCP tools.

Blocked characters in Bash commands: ; & | ` $ < > \ and newlines. This rules out pipes, chaining, redirection and substitution entirely; the skill uses the Grep tool for regex searches, %x09 separators in git --format, and BETWEEN in SQL.

Every denial is logged with a severity (low for the model's own formatting slips) and becomes a red flag when it happens in a service run.

docs.title: History access (nimi-sql)
docs.text:
Service runs let the skill query history with read-only SQL. The service names the command in a context block at the top of the input:

RCA context (from NIMI):
- Analyze only these subjects: orders.payments
- History SQL: /…/nimi-service/bin/nimi-sql "<one SQL statement>"
---
<the alert / log text>

The skill writes the SQL; the service only provides access:

  • Database boundary: it connects as nimi_skill_reader, which can read only skill_messages and skill_rcas (read-only sessions, 5s timeout).
  • The command runs one statement in a read-only transaction, returns at most 100 rows and 4000 characters per value, masks recognized secrets, and has no psql meta-commands (no shell, no file output).
  • Credentials: per run, the reader's password goes into a private temporary file (deleted afterwards); the run's environment carries its path and the non-secret settings, with NIMI_ENV=/dev/null so the command never reads the service's own settings.
  • The guard allows exactly that file from the same checkout, with the usual character rules, so the skill writes ranges with BETWEEN and avoids ;, <, >, |.

History is a guarded command rather than an MCP server on purpose: organizations often restrict MCP servers through managed Claude Code policies, while a command runs anywhere the skill does.

docs.title: Headless runs
docs.text:
The service runs, from the skill folder:

claude -p "/rca <input>" --settings .claude/nimi-session-settings.json \
  --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash,WebSearch,Skill --permission-mode dontAsk \
  --setting-sources user,project --strict-mcp-config --output-format json

with a clean environment (see Configuration) and a timeout of NIMI_RCA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. A run costs roughly $0.10–0.15 with Sonnet.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text: NIMI feeds untrusted text (alerts, logs, anything a system or person posts in a monitored channel) to language models that can read code. The design assumes that text may try to manipulate the model, and limits what any model can do regardless of what it is told.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
Actor Can Cannot RCA skill Read registered repos and its own folder; read-only git; plain-text web search; read-only SQL over two views. Write or modify anything; run other commands or scripts; open URLs (including links in alerts); read the service code, config or credentials; use MCP servers. Triage model Read the prompt the service builds. Use any tool. Service Read/write its database; read/post in registered channels as the configured user; call the admin webhook. (Code, not a model: it never executes model output.)

The skill's limits are enforced by the guard hook (allowlist, fails closed) and by Postgres permissions, not only by instructions. The service code, its settings and the reader's credentials live outside every path the guard allows.

docs.title: Untrusted input
docs.text:
• The skill and triage prompts mark message text as untrusted data. Only the service's context block at the very start of the skill's input is an instruction.
  • URLs in input are never opened: WebFetch is denied, and web searches may not contain URLs, domains or IPs, or any internal data.
  • Model output is only stored and posted as text; replies are masked for secret formats before posting.

docs.title: Sensitive data
docs.text:
There is no free-text redaction. Instead NIMI detects, records and alerts:

  • a code scanner runs before any model; critical secrets hold the request from all models;
  • triage and the skill report types (never values) of sensitive data they notice;
  • red flags record type and location only and notify the admin webhook;
  • the skill is instructed never to write sensitive values; outgoing replies are masked as a backstop.

See Red flags.

docs.title: Least-privilege database access
docs.text: Three roles: the service (owner), the skill reader (two views, read-only, 5s timeout), and an optional development review role (one view). Even unrestricted SQL from the skill can't read other tables, write, create objects, read server files or run longer than 5 seconds. See Data model.

docs.title: Claude environment
docs.text: Claude calls get a clean environment: unrelated API keys, base URLs or model overrides from the shell are not passed through; the account comes only from NIMI's settings. Triage loads no settings layers at all; RCA runs load user,project by default and no MCP servers. Your organization's managed policy always applies.

docs.title: Local machine
docs.text: NIMI writes only to its database, ~/.cache/nimi/ (triage working directory, per-run temporary files), project copies you opted into sync for (fetch + checkout, never when they have uncommitted changes or local commits), ~/.local/state/nimi/guard-denials.jsonl, and the Google Chat token when it refreshes (~/.config/nimi/gchat-token.json, chmod 600). Registered repos are only read; the skill can't read the token or any settings file.

docs.title: Triage
docs.text: Triage decides, for each new request, whether a fresh RCA is needed. It is a hybrid: a cheap model call makes the judgement, and code sets the limits and checks the answer.

docs.title: Inputs (assembled by the service)
docs.text:
• the new message (up to 6000 characters) and its time;
  • history: the 10 most recent earlier messages with the same signature within the reuse window, with their parsed status;
  • platform notes: confirmed facts from the platform profiles whose applies_to matches the message (trusted guidance, unlike the message data);
  • candidates: earlier RCAs for the same signature from the last NIMI_REUSE_DAYS (7) days, never ones rated 👎 and never the request's own earlier results (so a re-run doesn't just return its old answer), each with its input, analyzed subjects, a report excerpt and feedback.

The new message comes last in the prompt, labelled as the message to decide on: alert history is long and repetitive, and a small model reading it last tends to mistake earlier firings for the current one.

docs.title: What the model decides
docs.text:
Per subject (a table, dataset, service, deployment — not a pod — job, or *):

Decision Meaning reuse every subject is covered by a candidate RCA of the same ongoing incident new a fresh RCA (lists the subjects to analyze) partial some subjects reused, some new not_applicable no RCA: OK/resolved, informational, or a test message

Rules it follows include: a subject that recovered in between (an OK message, or a firing message that no longer listed it) is a new incident; an error log that hadn't appeared for about a day is a new incident; sender and webhook names are never evidence of a test; when unsure, run a fresh RCA. It also reports the types of any sensitive data in the message (never values).

docs.title: What code enforces
docs.text:
• Only candidates the service offered can be reused; IDs are checked.
  • Subjects must appear in the new message: any the model took from history are dropped (if none remain, the RCA covers the whole message).
  • Invalid or unparseable output falls back to a fresh RCA (and raises a red flag).
  • A Claude unavailability error pauses the service instead of falling back.

docs.title: Isolation
docs.text: The triage call has no tools at all: --tools "", no MCP servers, no slash commands, no settings layers, no session persistence, run from an empty working directory (~/.cache/nimi/triage) with a clean environment. It can't read files, run commands or browse; it only sees the prompt. Because secrets could be in the message, the code scanner runs first and holds requests with critical secrets before any model sees them.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: Triage uses NIMI_TRIAGE_MODEL (default haiku): about $0.001 per message. It is not counted against the daily RCA cap.

docs.title: Adding a provider
docs.text:
To support another chat platform (Slack, Teams, …):

  1. Create nimi_service/providers/<name>/ with:
    • a client with the platform's auth, rate limits and retry policy (see gchat/client.py: per-channel and per-project limiters, backoff on 429/5xx, posts not retried after a possible send);
    • rendering of payloads into readable rendered_text (cards, attachments, mentions);
    • a Provider subclass implementing every method in providers/base.py.
  2. Normalize carefully:
    • external_id must be unique per provider and stable;
    • set thread_external_id, and is_thread_reply for replies;
    • map sender types to bot / human (this decides what is ever analyzed);
    • normalize emoji so 👍 / 🤔 / 👎 match reactions.VERDICTS (strip skin tones).
  3. Register it in providers/__init__.py.
  4. Add its credentials as settings in config.py (plus env.example and the settings reference).
  5. Test normalization and rendering with real payloads (see the Google Chat tests in tests/test_parse.py), then on a scratch database: 
    .venv/bin/python -m nimi_service add-channel <name> <channel id> <label> --rca
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service ingest-once

Nothing else changes: the database, triage, the skill and the workflow are provider-neutral.

docs.title: Changing the skill
docs.text: The skill is plain files in nimi-skill/.claude/. Changes take effect on the next run; the service records a hash of the skill files (skill_version) with every result, so results can be compared across versions.

docs.title: Where to change what
docs.text:
To change Edit The investigation process, report rules, output contract skills/rca/SKILL.md The report layout skills/rca/templates/report.md Allowed sources (the list the skill follows) skills/rca/sources.md Which repos exist and how to pick one skills/rca/projects/ (Adding a project) What is technically allowed hooks/nimi_guard.py The subagent's model and tools agents/rca-investigator.md

Keep paths portable: refer to the skill's own files as ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/… in SKILL.md (Claude Code substitutes it), and to project paths as <name>/… resolved from registry.json.

docs.title: Changing the guard
docs.text:
The guard is the security boundary, so:

  • keep it an allowlist that fails closed (any exception denies);
  • prefer narrowing over widening; when widening, add tests in nimi-service/tests/ that cover both the newly allowed form and near-misses that must stay denied;
  • give denials actionable reasons (the model reads them) and mark the model's own formatting slips as low severity so they don't page anyone;
  • if the output contract changes, update rca.py (parse_output) and the reference together.

docs.title: Testing a change
docs.text:
1. Unit tests: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests.
  2. By hand: cd nimi-skill && claude, /rca <a real alert with a known cause>.
  3. Through the service on a scratch database: rca-text "<alert>" (includes history access and the session-wide guard).
  4. Check ~/.local/state/nimi/guard-denials.jsonl for unexpected denials.

When choosing models, compare correctness and cost on alerts with confirmed root causes. The subagent defaults to Sonnet: on such comparisons it has matched larger models on correctness at a fraction of the cost, but measure with your own alerts before changing it.

docs.title: Writing docs
docs.text: The documentation is plain Markdown in docs/, so it reads fine on GitHub, in an editor, or by an agent. MkDocs with the Material theme renders it as a website with navigation, search and diagrams.

docs.title: Preview and build
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv-docs
.venv-docs/bin/pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
.venv-docs/bin/mkdocs serve        # http://127.0.0.1:8000, reloads on save
.venv-docs/bin/mkdocs build        # static site in site/ (git-ignored)

The build runs in strict mode: broken links or pages missing from the navigation fail it.

Tool choice

MkDocs + Material because the project is Python (no Node toolchain) and the pages stay plain Markdown. docs/requirements.txt pins MkDocs below 2.0, which drops plugin and theme compatibility. If MkDocs 1.x becomes a problem, Zensical (by the Material team) builds the same mkdocs.yml and docs/ folder. Docusaurus also works, but needs Node 18+ and MDX-flavoured pages.

docs.title: Hosting
docs.text:
site/ is a static site; host it anywhere:

  • GitHub Pages: mkdocs gh-deploy (pushes the built site to the gh-pages branch).
  • Internal: copy site/ to any web server or bucket (nginx, GCS/S3 static hosting).
  • Locally: mkdocs serve, or open site/index.html.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Add new pages to nav in mkdocs.yml.
  • Diagrams: fenced ```mermaid blocks.
  • Notes and warnings: !!! note / !!! warning admonitions.
  • When you add a setting or CLI command, update Settings and CLI; tests fail if they are missing.
  • Keep the READMEs short and link here instead of duplicating content.

docs.title: Schema changes
docs.text: Tables are defined in nimi_service/models.py; views in nimi_service/views.py. Alembic migrations in nimi-service/db/migrations/versions/ apply them.

docs.title: Changing tables
docs.text:
# 1. edit nimi_service/models.py
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service db revision "add foo column"   # autogenerate a migration
# 2. review the generated file: autogenerate can miss renames, data changes, server defaults and
#    CHECK constraint changes
# 3. try it on a scratch database (see Developer setup), including downgrade
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service db upgrade
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service db current
  • Each migration runs in its own transaction; a failure rolls that migration back.
  • Never edit a migration that has been applied anywhere — add a new one. (Before any database existed, the history was squashed into 0001_baseline.py.)
  • CHECK constraints (e.g. allowed statuses) are not compared by autogenerate: drop and re-create them by hand in the migration.
  • Back up the real database before upgrading it.

docs.title: Changing views
docs.text:
Views aren't autogenerated. To change one:

  1. edit it in views.py;
  2. write a migration that calls drop_views(op, OLD) then create_views(op, NEW) with frozen copies of the old and new SQL inside the migration (so replaying old migrations never uses newer SQL);
  3. if it is one of SKILL_VIEWS, nothing else is needed: db upgrade re-grants the skill reader on every run. Re-run dev/review_access.sh for the review role.

docs.title: Checking for drift
docs.text: After an upgrade, db revision on an up-to-date database should produce an empty migration (delete it). Comparing pg_dump -s output before and after a refactor is a good way to prove nothing changed.
