docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
cd nimi-service
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests

Unit tests need no database or network. They cover parsing, triage validation, the guard hook, output parsing, formatting, settings, exclusions and history access.

docs.title: A scratch database
docs.text:
Use a throwaway Postgres container for anything touching the schema, so your real database is never involved:

docker run -d --rm --name nimi-test-db -p 127.0.0.1:5441:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=testpw postgres:18
PGPASSWORD=testpw psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5441 -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE nimi"

export NIMI_ENV=/dev/null NIMI_DB_PORT=5441 NIMI_DB_USER=postgres NIMI_DB_PASSWORD=testpw
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service db upgrade
# … test …
docker rm -f nimi-test-db

NIMI_ENV=/dev/null makes sure none of your real settings files are read.

docs.title: Reviewing stored data
docs.text:
To let someone (or an agent) review stored messages without the service's read-write credentials:

bash dev/review_access.sh            # creates nimi_readonly: SELECT on review_messages and skill_rcas only; password in ~/.pgpass
bash dev/review_access.sh revoke     # removes it

Re-run it after migrations that recreate views (dropping a view drops its grants).

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
See also CONTRIBUTING.md at the repository root (pull requests, licensing, the no-real-data rule). CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs the tests on Python 3.10–3.12 and the strict docs build.

  • Settings: add a field to Settings and an entry to ENV_VARS in config.py, a line to env.example, and a row to the settings reference (a test checks this).
  • CLI commands: add them to the module docstring of __main__.py and to the CLI reference (a test checks this).
  • Never log or store secret values; red flags carry types and locations only.
  • Model calls go through claude_cli.build_env (clean environment).
  • Keep the provider interface neutral: nothing outside providers/ may know about a specific platform.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All settings are environment-style NIMI_* variables. The complete list with defaults is in the settings reference; nimi-service/env.example is a commented template.

docs.title: Where settings come from
docs.text:
Later sources override earlier ones:

  1. built-in defaults
  2. ~/.config/nimi/service.env — outside the repo (created by db/bootstrap.sh)
  3. nimi-service/.env — inside the repo folder, git-ignored (easy to find)
  4. real environment variables

NIMI_ENV=/path/to/file replaces 2 and 3 with exactly that file. To check what is in effect and where each value came from (secrets masked):

.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service config

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Connection details are separate settings — not a URL — so credentials can be injected from a secrets manager (Vault Agent, Kubernetes secrets, …):

Setting Default NIMI_DB_HOST / NIMI_DB_PORT / NIMI_DB_NAME 127.0.0.1 / 5432 / nimi NIMI_DB_USER nimi_service NIMI_DB_PASSWORD or NIMI_DB_PASSWORD_FILE unset: libpq falls back to ~/.pgpass / trust / peer auth NIMI_DB_SSLMODE unset (e.g. require for managed Postgres) NIMI_DB_SKILL_USER nimi_skill_reader NIMI_DB_SKILL_PASSWORD or NIMI_DB_SKILL_PASSWORD_FILE unset

docs.title: Which Claude account NIMI uses
docs.text:
Triage and RCA runs start claude with a clean environment: variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL exported in your shell for other work are not passed through. Only these settings decide:

Setting Effect NIMI_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR A separate Claude login and user config, e.g. ~/.claude-nimi (log in once with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-nimi claude). Unset = your default ~/.claude. Keep it outside the repo: it holds login tokens. NIMI_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_FILE Use an API key read from this file (API billing) instead of the stored login. NIMI_CLAUDE_SETTING_SOURCES Settings layers RCA runs load: default user,project. project ignores your user-level settings, skills and plugins. Triage never loads any. NIMI_CLAUDE_PASS_ENV Extra variables to pass through, e.g. HTTPS_PROXY,NO_PROXY. NIMI_CLAUDE_BIN The claude executable (default: claude on PATH).

With nothing set, everything uses your normal login and ~/.claude config. Your organization's managed Claude Code policy always applies on top.

docs.title: Settings you are most likely to change
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning NIMI_POST_ENABLED false Post replies to chat. Off = dry run (results are stored, not posted). NIMI_POST_TARGET / NIMI_POST_WEBHOOK thread / unset Reply in the alert's thread, in a separate space via an incoming webhook, or both (Where replies go). NIMI_ADMIN_WEBHOOK unset Incoming webhook of the admin's chat space for red flags. NIMI_ALERT_SENDERS any bot Comma-separated sender IDs allowed to trigger RCAs. NIMI_STALE_HOURS 6 Alerts older than this when NIMI can process them get no RCA. NIMI_MAX_PER_DAY / NIMI_MAX_PARALLEL 50 / 2 Daily cap on RCA runs (UTC) / concurrent runs. NIMI_TRIAGE_MODEL haiku Model for triage. NIMI_SKILL_HISTORY true Let RCA runs query past messages and RCAs. NIMI_REPLY_DISCLAIMER built-in The disclaimer on the first line of every RCA message (👁️ NIMI — <disclaimer>), e.g. to say where NIMI runs.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Secret values (NIMI_DB_PASSWORD, NIMI_DB_SKILL_PASSWORD, NIMI_ADMIN_WEBHOOK, NIMI_POST_WEBHOOK) are masked by config and never logged. Prefer the *_FILE variants with a secrets manager. Never put real values in env.example: it is committed.

docs.title: First run
docs.text: Assumes Installation is done. All commands run from nimi-service/.

docs.title: 1. Register channels
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service add-channel gchat AAAAxxxxxxx alerts --rca --display-name team-alerts
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service add-channel gchat AAAAyyyyyyy app-logs          # logs: history/context only
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service channels
  • The channel ID is the space ID (AAAA… or spaces/AAAA…); the label is your short name for it.
  • --rca enables RCAs for the channel. Without it, messages are still ingested and visible to the skill as history (e.g. register a logs space without --rca to use its logs as context for alert RCAs), but never analyzed themselves.
  • Running add-channel again for a registered channel updates it in place: --rca / --no-rca switch RCAs on or off (from new messages on); options you leave out keep their current values.
  • --backfill-days N sets how much history the first poll pulls (default NIMI_BACKFILL_DAYS, 90).

docs.title: 2. Ingest once (backfill)
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service ingest-once
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service status

The first poll of each channel pulls its history. Backfilled messages never trigger RCAs: they are history for triage and the skill. Later polls fetch only new messages.

docs.title: 3. Exclude known noise (optional)
docs.text:
Look at what arrives and exclude messages that never need an RCA:

.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service exclude add --like <message id> --reason "ticket reminder, no failure"

See Messages that don't need an RCA.

docs.title: 4. Try an RCA on one message
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service rca <provider message id>     # e.g. spaces/AAAA…/messages/…

This runs triage and the skill now and prints the result. Nothing is posted while NIMI_POST_ENABLED=false.

docs.title: 5. Run the service
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service run

Every NIMI_POLL_SECONDS (60) it recovers stuck runs, ingests new messages, triages, runs queued RCAs (up to NIMI_MAX_PARALLEL), posts replies (if enabled), syncs reactions, and retries red-flag notifications. Stop it with Ctrl-C; running RCAs finish first. After a restart it continues where it stopped (Operating the service).

docs.title: 6. Turn on posting
docs.text: When you are happy with the stored results, set NIMI_POST_ENABLED=true and restart. Replies go into the alert's thread by default; to send them to a separate space instead (or as well), see Where replies go.

docs.title: Google Chat access
docs.text:
NIMI reads (and, when enabled, posts) in Google Chat as your user, with an OAuth token that you create once. It doesn't use a bot or a service account: it sees exactly the spaces you are in, and its thread replies appear as posted by you (with NIMI's header and disclaimer).

You need a Google Cloud project, an OAuth client for it, and one browser login. Google renames console menus now and then; the steps below say what to do rather than exact menu paths.

docs.title: 1. Google Cloud project
docs.text: Use a project in your organization's Google Cloud (ideally one owned by your team rather than a personal project), or create one. You need permission to enable APIs and create OAuth clients in it.

docs.title: 2. Enable the Google Chat API
docs.text: In the project's API library, enable Google Chat API.

docs.title: 3. Configure the Chat app
docs.text: Google requires a Chat app configuration in the project before the Chat API can be used, even with user credentials. In the Chat API's Configuration page, fill in the minimum: app name (e.g. NIMI), an avatar URL and a description. NIMI doesn't run as a Chat app, so it doesn't need to be published or added to any space. Without this step, API calls fail with an error saying the Chat app was not found.

docs.title: 4. OAuth consent screen
docs.text:
Set up the project's OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform):

  • Audience: Internal if the project belongs to your Google Workspace organization. Only users in your organization can log in, and no Google verification is needed.
  • External works too, but while the app is in Testing you must add yourself as a test user, and Google expires refresh tokens after 7 days in that state — the service would stop being able to refresh its token every week. Prefer Internal.
  • Scopes (optional to declare here; the login requests them anyway): https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chat.spaces.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chat.messages.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chat.messages.create.

docs.title: 5. Create an OAuth client
docs.text: Create an OAuth client ID of application type Desktop app, and download its JSON file (named like client_secret_<id>.apps.googleusercontent.com.json). Keep it private; you only need it for logging in.

docs.title: 6. Log in
docs.text:
On a machine with a browser, from nimi-service/:

.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service gchat-login --client-secret ~/Downloads/client_secret_XXXX.json

A browser opens (if not, open the URL it prints). Log in with the account NIMI should act as and accept the three permissions. The token is saved to ~/.config/nimi/gchat-token.json (chmod 600), or to NIMI_GCHAT_TOKEN_FILE if set. The token contains what it needs to refresh itself, so you can delete the downloaded client file now.

Server without a browser? Run gchat-login on your own machine, then copy the token file to the server (same path or NIMI_GCHAT_TOKEN_FILE) and chmod 600 it.

docs.title: 7. Check it
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service gchat-spaces          # named spaces and their IDs; --all adds direct messages

Note the IDs of the spaces to monitor (spaces/AAAA…) for First run.

docs.title: What the token can do
docs.text:
Scope Used for chat.spaces.readonly Listing spaces and reading their details chat.messages.readonly Reading messages, thread replies and reactions chat.messages.create Posting RCA replies (only when NIMI_POST_ENABLED=true)

It can't edit or delete messages or manage spaces or members. It can read every space you can see; the service only polls the channels you register.

Treat the token like a password. Anyone with the file can read your chats and post as you until access is revoked. It lives outside the repo, and the RCA skill can't read it.

docs.title: Keeping it working
docs.text:
The service refreshes the access token automatically (about hourly) and writes the refreshed token back. It never opens a browser: if the token can't be refreshed, it stops and tells you to log in again. Run gchat-login again when:

  • you revoke NIMI's access, or change the account's password (Google may revoke tokens then);
  • the OAuth client is deleted or its secret is reset;
  • the app is External and in Testing (tokens expire after 7 days);
  • the token has not been used for about six months;
  • NIMI's required scopes change (the service reports "lacks required scopes").

To revoke access: Google Account → Security → third-party connections → remove the app.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause and fix … not found: log in with … gchat-login … No token at NIMI_GCHAT_TOKEN_FILE: run gchat-login. … lacks required scopes The token was created with other scopes: run gchat-login again. … is invalid and cannot be refreshed / invalid_grant Token revoked or expired (see the list above): run gchat-login again. Error mentioning that the Chat app was not found Step 3 is missing: configure the Chat app in the project. Login page says access is blocked or needs admin approval Your Workspace admin restricts third-party apps: ask them to allow the OAuth client ID (or use an Internal app in an organization project). 403 / 404 for a specific space Your account isn't a member of that space (or it was deleted). 429 warnings in the log Rate limiting: the client already backs off and retries; see Messaging providers.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This page sets everything up once: the projects the skill analyzes, the Python environment, Google Chat access, Claude, and the database. Then continue with First run.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: What Notes Linux or macOS, git Python 3.10+ 3.11+ recommended (Google's client libraries are dropping 3.10). PostgreSQL 13+ Tested on 18. Local or managed. The pg_trgm extension must be available (it ships with Postgres). Claude Code CLI Logged in (claude, then /login), or an API key — see Configuration. Local checkouts of the repos to analyze E.g. your service repos. Read-only use: NIMI never modifies them. A Google Cloud OAuth client for the Chat API Desktop-app OAuth client (client_secret.json) with the Chat API enabled. Only needed for the service, not for running /rca by hand.

docs.title: 1. Get the code
docs.text:
git clone <nimi repo> ~/nimi        # any location works; nothing depends on the path
cd ~/nimi

docs.title: 2. Register the projects the skill may read
docs.text:
The skill may only read code inside registered project paths (enforced by its guard hook).

cd nimi-skill/.claude/skills/rca/projects
cp -r example local
# edit local/registry.json (absolute checkout paths), local/INDEX.md and one local/<name>.md per project

Everything in projects/local/ describes your systems and is git-ignored; projects/example/ is the template. See Adding a project.

At this point the skill already works by hand: cd nimi-skill && claude, then /rca <alert text> — see Running an RCA by hand. The rest of this page is for the service.

docs.title: 3. Python environment
docs.text:
cd nimi-service
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests          # optional: should pass

docs.title: 4. Google Chat access
docs.text:
NIMI reads (and, when enabled, posts) as your user with an OAuth token. Follow Google Chat access: enable the Chat API in a Google Cloud project, configure the Chat app and the consent screen, create a Desktop app OAuth client, then log in once:

.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service gchat-login --client-secret ~/Downloads/client_secret_XXXX.json
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service gchat-spaces          # note the IDs of your alert and log spaces

docs.title: Local Postgres: db/bootstrap.sh
docs.text:
bash nimi-service/db/bootstrap.sh          # uses sudo -u postgres for CREATE ROLE / DATABASE

It creates:

  • the service role (nimi_service), owner of the database (nimi) and the only role that can create objects;
  • the skill reader role (nimi_skill_reader): read-only, used by the skill's history queries;
  • ~/.config/nimi/service.env (chmod 600) with the connection settings and generated passwords (never printed).

To write the settings into the repo folder instead (nimi-service/.env, git-ignored, read by the service and overriding ~/.config/nimi/service.env):

NIMI_ENV_FILE_OUT=~/nimi/nimi-service/.env bash nimi-service/db/bootstrap.sh

Names are configurable: NIMI_DB_NAME=rca NIMI_DB_USER=rca_svc NIMI_DB_SKILL_USER=rca_skill bash …. The script is safe to re-run with the same NIMI_ENV_FILE_OUT (it reads names and passwords back from that file and re-syncs the role passwords). Passwords are handed to psql on standard input, never as command-line arguments.

docs.title: Managed Postgres / infrastructure as code
docs.text:
Skip the script. Create:

  1. a database and a login role that owns it (the service role);
  2. a second login role for the skill reader with default_transaction_read_only = on, statement_timeout = '5s', CONNECT on the database and nothing else;

then set the NIMI_DB_* settings (Configuration). Passwords can come from a secrets manager (NIMI_DB_PASSWORD_FILE, NIMI_DB_SKILL_PASSWORD_FILE) or ~/.pgpass.

docs.title: Create the schema
docs.text:
cd nimi-service
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service db upgrade

This creates all tables and views and grants the skill reader access to its two views. Re-run it after pulling changes that include migrations.

docs.title: 6. Check the configuration
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service config      # every setting, its value (secrets masked) and source
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service db current  # schema version: should say "up to date"

Next: First run.

docs.title: Adding a project to analyze
docs.text:
A project is a code repository (or several) the skill may read for RCAs, e.g. a backend monorepo or a dashboarding tool. Your projects live in nimi-skill/.claude/skills/rca/projects/local/ (git-ignored: it describes your systems). projects/example/ is a committed template with two sample projects; start with cp -r example local.

File in projects/local/ Purpose registry.json Project keys, descriptions, the default, each project's absolute checkout path(s), and optionally display_name, web_url and sync (below). The guard hook reads it: only these paths (plus the skill folder) are readable, and git -C may only target them. Missing or invalid: nothing is readable (fail closed). INDEX.md How the skill picks a project from an alert: signals per project, the default, what to do when nothing matches. Without it the skill replies insufficient_context. <name>.md Per-project guide: repo layout, where to orient first, config and dependency files, runbook locations, project-specific notes. Paths are written as <name>/…, meaning the project's path from the registry.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone the repo into a NIMI-only folder (see below: not your working copy).
  2. Add the project to projects/local/registry.json with its real absolute path: 
    "billing": {
  "description": "Billing service: invoices, payment webhooks, reconciliation jobs",
  "paths": ["/home/you/nimi-copies/billing"],
  "display_name": "acme/billing",
  "sync": "origin/main"
}
  3. Write projects/local/billing.md following projects/example/shop.md: path placeholder, how to orient, where code and config live, dependency files, runbook locations.
  4. Add a row to projects/local/INDEX.md with the signals that identify it in alerts (package names, service names, alert senders).
  5. Test with /rca on a real alert from that system.

docs.title: Use a dedicated copy, and keep it current
docs.text:
Point the registry at a checkout used only by NIMI (e.g. ~/nimi-copies/shop), not your working copy: local commits or uncommitted changes there would make RCAs describe code that isn't deployed. A copy goes stale unless something updates it; each report records the commit it analyzed, but stale code still means weaker RCAs. Two ways to keep it current:

  • Let NIMI sync it (opt-in): add "sync": "origin/main" (<remote>/<branch>) to the project. Between RCA runs, at most every NIMI_SYNC_MINUTES (10), the service fetches and moves the copy to that ref. It never touches a checkout with uncommitted changes or local commits: it skips it and raises a red flag, so an accidentally registered working copy can't lose anything. The RCA skill itself stays read-only.
  • Do it yourself, e.g. a cron job, if you prefer NIMI never to change anything: 
    */15 * * * *  git -C ~/nimi-copies/shop fetch -q origin main && git -C ~/nimi-copies/shop checkout -q --detach origin/main

docs.title: How projects appear in RCAs
docs.text:
People know a repository by its name, not by your local folder, so the RCA:

  • names projects by display_name (e.g. acme/shop; default: the registry key) and files by their path in the repo: acme/shop: services/api/checkout.py:88. Absolute local paths are rewritten this way before anything is posted, so your folder layout never reaches chat;
  • links cited code to the file at the analyzed commit on the code host (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and GitHub-like hosts). The base URL is web_url, or is derived from the copy's origin remote (credentials in remote URLs are dropped). Without one, citations stay plain text.
"shop": {
  "paths": ["/home/you/nimi-copies/shop"],
  "display_name": "acme/shop",
  "web_url": "https://github.com/acme/shop",
  "sync": "origin/main"
}

docs.title: Runbooks and alert docs
docs.text: Runbooks are hints, never proof: the skill must find them, label claims from them as unverified, check their age, and never perform their actions. The best place to document what an alert means is the project's own repo (e.g. docs/runbooks/); list that location in the project file.

docs.title: When Claude is unavailable
docs.text:
If a Claude call fails with a usage-limit, rate-limit, credit, budget or login error, the service pauses all Claude calls. The pause is stored in service_state, so it survives restarts.

During a pause:

  • requests stay in triage / queued; the failed attempt doesn't count. Ingestion keeps running.
  • one red flag is raised for the episode (critical if an admin must act: credit, budget, login).
  • each pending alert's thread gets a short notice, once, that NIMI couldn't analyze it because its Claude usage limit was reached. The notice makes no promise of a later RCA, and OK/resolved messages get none.

The pause ends at Claude's reset time if the error includes one, otherwise after NIMI_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MINUTES (15). Then pending alerts older than NIMI_STALE_HOURS are skipped and the rest are triaged as usual; their RCA is posted in the same thread.

.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service status    # shows an active pause, its kind and until when
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service resume    # clear it now (e.g. after topping up credit or logging in)
Error kind Clears by itself Needs an admin usage_limit (subscription limit) yes, at reset rate_limit yes credit, budget yes auth (not logged in, invalid key) yes

A report without its closing RCA_FIELDS block (cut short by a limit or crash) is an error, never a finished RCA. "Not logged in" responses that the CLI reports as successful are detected too.

docs.title: Rating replies
docs.text:
React to an RCA reply in the chat thread:

Reaction Verdict 👍 correct 🤔 partially right 👎 wrong

Replies posted in the last NIMI_REACTION_DAYS (7) days are re-checked every 10 minutes, wherever they were posted (posts in a webhook space count too, if the token's account can read it). Reactions are stored in reactions and turned into rca_feedback rows; removing a reaction marks its feedback removed. Skin-tone variants count the same.

Feedback is used in three places:

  • Reuse: an RCA rated 👎 is never reused.
  • The skill's history: previous RCAs come with their feedback counts, and the skill is told to treat ones rated wrong with distrust.
  • Quality tracking: the rca_feedback_summary view.

docs.title: When an earlier RCA is reused
docs.text:
Alerts often repeat while an incident is ongoing. Instead of a new RCA for each repeat, triage can reuse an earlier one per subject (a table, service, deployment or job the message is about):

  • only RCAs for messages with the same signature,
  • from the last NIMI_REUSE_DAYS (7) days,
  • never one rated 👎,
  • never one from an rca --no-post run (nobody saw it, and the reply couldn't link to it),
  • and only if it is the same ongoing incident: if history shows the subject recovered in between (an OK message, or a firing message that no longer listed it), it is a new incident and gets a fresh RCA.

A reused reply says which earlier RCA covers the alert, links to it and repeats its TL;DR. When only some subjects are covered, the fresh RCA analyzes just the new ones and the reply lists both ("partial"). When in doubt, triage runs a fresh RCA: a wrong reuse is worse than an extra RCA.

docs.title: In Claude Code (no service needed)
docs.text:
cd nimi-skill
claude

Then paste the alert or log text after /rca:

/rca [Alerting] Order export delayed
Tables with no new data for 6h: orders, order_items

The skill runs in a forked rca-investigator subagent under the guard hook (read-only, registered projects only). It ends with a report and an RCA_FIELDS block (output contract). History lookups are not available here: they are provided only by the service.

docs.title: Through the service
docs.text:
Both commands store the request and result in the database, like automatic RCAs:

# A stored message, by its provider ID: triage first (may reuse an earlier RCA), then the skill
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service rca spaces/AAAA…/messages/…
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service rca spaces/AAAA…/messages/… --fresh   # always a new RCA: no reuse, no exclusion rules
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service rca spaces/AAAA…/messages/… --no-post # store it, never post it

# Any text (a manual request: no triage, no channel, nothing posted)
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service rca-text "<alert or log text>"

Manual text is scanned for secrets first (a red flag is raised if any are found). Service runs include history access when NIMI_SKILL_HISTORY=true.

docs.title: Reading the result
docs.text:
To look at a stored RCA again (automatic or manual) without starting a new run:

.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service show spaces/AAAA…/messages/…          # request + latest report
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service show spaces/AAAA…/messages/… --chat   # the chat message instead
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service show spaces/AAAA…/messages/… --render   # rendered now, current layout, nothing left out
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service show 42 --all                         # by request ID, every attempt

The printed result shows outcome, cost, duration, model, origin, confidence and self-healing, followed by the report. Outcomes:

Outcome Meaning rca A report. not_applicable The skill found nothing to analyze (e.g. a resolved message). insufficient_context Not enough signal; the reason says what is missing. error / timeout The run failed or was cut short. A report without its closing RCA_FIELDS block counts as an error.

docs.title: Operating the service
docs.text: Commands run from nimi-service/ as .venv/bin/python -m nimi_service <command>. The full list is in the CLI reference.

docs.title: The poll loop
docs.text:
run repeats every NIMI_POLL_SECONDS (default 60):

  1. Recover stuck runs: requests left running longer than NIMI_RCA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS + 60s go back to the queue, or to failed after max_attempts (2).
  2. Ingest new messages from every channel (first poll of a channel backfills).
  3. Schedule:
    • post replies that finished but were never posted (outbox sweep);
    • if Claude is paused, stop here;
    • skip requests older than NIMI_STALE_HOURS;
    • triage waiting requests (up to 20 per cycle);
    • start queued RCAs, up to NIMI_MAX_PARALLEL at once and NIMI_MAX_PER_DAY per UTC day.
  4. Reactions: sync 👍 / 🤔 / 👎 on replies posted in the last NIMI_REACTION_DAYS.
  5. Red flags: retry notifications that failed to send.

A failing cycle raises a red flag and the loop carries on.

docs.title: Request lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> triage: new bot message in an RCA channel
    [*] --> skipped: stale / sender not allowed / exclusion rule
    triage --> held: critical secret in the message
    held --> triage: release
    triage --> skipped: exclusion rule added later / stale
    triage --> not_applicable: OK, informational, test
    triage --> reused: same incident as an earlier RCA
    triage --> queued: needs a fresh RCA (fully or partly)
    queued --> running
    queued --> skipped: daily cap / stale
    running --> done
    running --> queued: interrupted (retry)
    running --> failed: errors after max attempts

reused, not_applicable, done, skipped and failed are final. Every skip has a skip_reason.

docs.title: Watching it
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service status       # channels, message counts, request states, active pause
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service red-flags    # things an admin should look at
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service exclude      # exclusion rules and their hit counts

Logs go to stderr (INFO level): each poll's counts, triage decisions, RCA runs with cost and duration.

docs.title: Restarts and downtime
docs.text:
Progress lives in Postgres, so after a restart (even a long one) the service continues where it stopped:

  • Messages: each channel's watermark makes the first poll fetch everything posted while it was down (with overlap_seconds of overlap so nothing is missed).
  • One age rule: alerts older than NIMI_STALE_HOURS (default 6) when NIMI can process them get no RCA — whether they arrived during downtime, waited in the queue across a shutdown, or waited out a usage-limit pause (skip_reason: "stale: alert older than …").
  • Interrupted runs go back to the queue (subject to the age rule).
  • Missed replies: an RCA or reuse decision that finished but was never posted is posted by the outbox sweep on the next poll, if the alert is still within NIMI_STALE_HOURS.

docs.title: Running it permanently
docs.text:
NIMI has no packaged service unit yet. A systemd user unit like this works:

# ~/.config/systemd/user/nimi.service
[Unit]
Description=NIMI RCA service
After=network-online.target

[Service]
WorkingDirectory=%h/nimi/nimi-service
ExecStart=%h/nimi/nimi-service/.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service run
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=30

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target

systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now nimi
journalctl --user -u nimi -f

docs.title: Maintenance tasks
docs.text: Task Command Pull older history for a channel backfill <channel> --days N (stored as backfill: no RCAs; safe to re-run) Rebuild parses/signatures after changing parse.py or a platform profile Check with parse-test, then reparse (bump RULES_VERSION in parse.py for code changes; profile changes are versioned automatically). Also moves RCA requests to their message's new signature, so earlier RCAs stay reusable, and warns about exclusion rules whose signature no longer exists. Clear a Claude pause now resume Send a held request to triage anyway release <request_id> Keep project copies current "sync" in the registry, or a cron job (Adding a project) Back up the database pg_dump -h 127.0.0.1 -U nimi_service nimi > nimi-$(date +%F).sql Apply new migrations after pulling db upgrade (back up first)

docs.title: Platform profiles
docs.text:
A platform profile (nimi-service/parsers/local/<name>.yaml, git-ignored) teaches NIMI about one platform's messages without code changes:

  • log layouts: how the platform's log lines look, so logs get a proper service, logger, title and signature;
  • subject masks: platform-specific item names to leave out of signatures;
  • triage notes: facts that help triage, shown only for messages they apply to.

Profiles are data (patterns). Yours live in parsers/local/, which is git-ignored because it describes your platforms; parsers/examples/example.yaml is a documented sample that is never loaded (copy it to local/ to start). The service is the only thing that reads profiles; the RCA skill always works from the full message text. With no profiles at all, the generic parse still works.

docs.title: Why signatures matter
docs.text: The parser gives each message a signature, its "kind of message". Triage only sees history and earlier RCAs with the same signature, and exclude --like matches by signature. If a format isn't recognised, the generic fallback still groups messages (masking numbers, IDs, timestamps, pod suffixes, Java object hashes such as Order@1b6d3586, hosts and common item names), so nothing breaks: the cost is extra RCAs, never wrong ones. A layout makes the grouping precise and the titles readable.

docs.title: How messages are matched
docs.text:
Every message is tried against the layouts of all profiles, regardless of channel, because one channel can carry messages from several platforms and formats. Layouts are tried in priority order (lower first; default 100, then file and list order); the first layout whose header matches a line wins. Messages no layout matches get the generic parse.

When two platforms' lines look alike:

  • same fields in the same places: it doesn't matter which layout matches; the service still comes from the pod/service name in the line;
  • similar shape, different meaning: narrow a layout with when: (sender display names, or text it must contain) and/or give it a lower priority.

docs.title: Writing a profile
docs.text:
name: myplatform                           # short lowercase id
description: Example services logging with a common Java/logback layout

log_layouts:
  - name: level-first
    # [ERROR] [2026-01-15 10:04:31+0000] [shop-api-deployment-7f8e9d0c1b-abcde] [checkout-3] com.example.shop.api.CheckoutController Payment failed …
    header: '^\[(?P<level>ERROR|WARN|FATAL)\]\s*\[(?P<ts>[^\]]+)\]\s*\[(?P<pod>[^\]]+)\](?:\s*\[[^\]]*\])*\s+(?P<logger>[\w$]+(?:\.[\w$]+)+)\s+(?P<message>.*)$'
    message: same_line                     # the error text is on the header line (next_lines: on the lines after)
    # when: {sender: ["Shop API Errors"], contains: ["com.example.shop"]}
    # priority: 50

subject_masks:                             # replaced by <name> in signatures
  - '(?<=for cart )[\w-]+'                 # "Payment failed for cart c-17 …"

triage_notes:
  - applies_to: {text_contains: ["Stock Sync Reminder"]}
    note: >-
      "Stock Sync Reminder" asks the warehouse team to confirm a manual stock sync; it reports no system
      failure.
Key Meaning header Regular expression (case-insensitive) matched against each line of the message. Named groups: pod or service (required; a pod's generated suffix is stripped to get the service), logger, level, message. message next_lines (default): the error is the first exception line after the header. same_line: the message group. when Optional. sender: display names; contains: texts the message must contain (any). priority Optional integer, lower first (default 100). subject_masks Regular expressions for item names (databases, tenants, …) to mask in signatures. triage_notes applies_to.text_contains (required; any of, case-insensitive) and note.

The signature of a log is log|<service>|<logger>|<error text with items masked>.

Triage notes are shown to the triage model as trusted guidance from NIMI's maintainers. Write only confirmed facts that help decide reuse vs new vs not applicable, e.g. "this alert lists only newly affected tables" or "this alert is a reminder, not a failure". Root causes and runbook knowledge belong in the project's repo docs, where the RCA skill finds them. The code limits on reuse (only offered candidates, never one rated 👎, the reuse window) always apply.

docs.title: Testing and applying a change
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service parse-test --text "<a log line or alert>"     # one message, plus matching notes
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service parse-test --channel app-logs --kind other      # stored messages still unmatched
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service parse-test --sender "Shop API Errors" --limit 5
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service reparse                                        # apply to all stored messages

parse-test writes nothing. For stored messages it shows which layout matched, the title and signature (with the current one when it would change), and a summary: layouts used, distinct signatures, and how many messages reparse would change.

A profile is validated when the service starts; an invalid one (unknown key, bad regex, missing group) stops it with the file and location. The parser version includes a hash of all profiles, so stored parses show which profile version produced them; run reparse after every profile change.

docs.title: Red flags
docs.text: NIMI doesn't try to redact free text. It detects, records and alerts a human instead. Flags are stored in red_flags (deduplicated, and never containing a sensitive value) and sent to the admin's chat space via NIMI_ADMIN_WEBHOOK.

docs.title: What raises a flag
docs.text:
Source Raises a flag when Kind scanner (code, before any model) a high-confidence secret format is in the message: private keys, cloud/API keys, tokens, password=…, credentials in URLs. Critical hits are held from all models until release. sensitive_data triage model it reports sensitive data in the message (types only) sensitive_data RCA skill it reports sensitive data in the input, code, config, logs, docs or history (sensitive_data: in RCA_FIELDS) sensitive_data guard hook it blocked a tool call (logged to ~/.local/state/nimi/guard-denials.jsonl, matched to the run by session ID). Formatting slips are recorded as low without a notification. rule_violation service triage failure, RCA error or timeout, posting / ingest / reaction failure, daily cap reached, Claude unavailable error

Repeats of the same problem bump occurrences on the open flag instead of notifying again.

docs.title: Replies are still posted
docs.text:
Sensitive data doesn't block replies (except critical secrets, which are held before any model sees them):

  • the skill never writes sensitive values, only their type and location;
  • outgoing text is masked for high-confidence formats as a backstop (and flagged if anything was masked);
  • a visible note asks the alert owner to remove the data from the source and rotate exposed credentials.

docs.title: Handling flags
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service red-flags                     # open flags
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service red-flags --all               # include resolved / ignored
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service red-flags resolve 12 --note "rotated the key"
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service red-flags resolve 13 --ignore --note "test data"
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service release 42                    # send a held request to triage anyway

docs.title: Messages that don't need an RCA
docs.text:
Only new, top-level bot messages in channels registered with --rca are considered at all. Human messages, thread replies and backfilled history are stored but never analyzed. Of the rest, several layers make sure RCAs (and their cost) go to messages that report a real problem.

Layer Who decides Cost Outcome Age: older than NIMI_STALE_HOURS code none skipped ("stale: …") Sender allowlist NIMI_ALERT_SENDERS (if set) code none skipped Exclusion rules code none skipped ("excluded by rule #id: reason") OK / resolved, informational, test messages triage model one cheap call not_applicable

Excluded and declined messages are still stored and still visible to the skill's history.

docs.title: Exclusion rules
docs.text:
A rule matches a message when every field it sets matches; unset fields match anything.

Option Matches --like <message> the same signature as that stored message (internal or provider message ID) --signature <key> exact signature key --channel <label> the channel --sender <id> exact sender ID, e.g. users/123 (see the note below) --title <text> case-insensitive substring of the parsed title (or the first line of the text) --status <status> parsed status, e.g. Alerting (case-insensitive) --text <text> case-insensitive substring of the message's full text, e.g. a service or host name that the parser keeps out of the title

A signature is the parser's coarse "kind of message": varying parts such as numbers, IDs, timestamps and masked subjects are removed, so all occurrences of the same alert share it. The service matches it in code; no model is involved. Because it is coarse, --like can cover more than one specific alert (e.g. the same alert type for every table), so exclude add always previews the signature and the stored messages it would have matched, and asks before saving. Narrow it with the other options if it's too broad.

# "stop doing RCAs for messages like this one"
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service exclude add --like spaces/AAAA…/messages/… \
    --reason "Ticket reminder: new tickets waiting to be claimed; no failure"

# temporary mute while a known issue is being fixed
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service exclude add --channel alerts --title "disk usage" \
    --reason "infra resizing volumes this week" --expires 7d

# every memory alert from the batch hosts, whatever the exact host
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service exclude add --text "batch-worker" --title "memory usage" \
    --reason "batch hosts: memory peaks during nightly jobs are expected"

.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service exclude              # active rules with hits and last hit
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service exclude list --all   # include disabled / expired
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service exclude disable 3
.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service exclude enable 3
  • A reason is required; --expires takes 7d, 12h, 30m or an ISO time.
  • Rules also apply to requests already waiting for triage when the rule is added (for example a backlog after a usage-limit pause).
  • Messages without a signature (unparsed) can't be used with --like; use the other options.
  • Google Chat incoming webhooks share one sender ID: messages from different webhooks (e.g. "Alerts test", "Grafana", every log webhook) all come from the same users/… ID, so --sender and NIMI_ALERT_SENDERS can't tell them apart. Use --like, --title or --channel instead.
  • After a parser change, reparse warns about rules whose signature no longer exists; re-create them with --like.
  • Review hit counts now and then: a rule with an unexpectedly high count may be too broad; one with no hits for months may be obsolete.

docs.title: What triage declines
docs.text:
The triage model (no tools; see Triage) returns not_applicable for:

  • OK / resolved messages ("[OK] …", "changed status to OK");
  • informational messages that report no failure: ticket/workflow reminders, periodic summaries, "job finished", deploy or maintenance notices (reason starts with informational:);
  • test messages: notification-channel tests (e.g. Grafana TestAlert), "test alert, please ignore", [TEST] … (reason starts with test:).

Safeguards:

  • A message that reports an error, a missed threshold, missing or late data, or degraded service is never informational, however routine.
  • A real failure that merely mentions test, staging or QA (a table, job or environment name) is not a test.
  • Sender, webhook, bot and space names are never evidence: a webhook called "Alerts test" that carries production alerts still gets RCAs.
  • When unsure, triage chooses an RCA.

Every decision's reason is stored (rca_requests.triage_reason). If triage declines something it shouldn't, tell us; if it keeps analyzing something harmless, add an exclusion rule.

docs.title: The message
docs.text:
Each RCA is one chat message; the full report stays in the database. The skill fills in the message's fields in simple words, as JSON (see skills/rca/templates/chat.md and the output contract); NIMI lays them out in a fixed order with fixed section names and adds the first line (👁️ NIMI — + the disclaimer, in italics), the RCA: title line, the status line and the rating line:

👁️ NIMI — Automated RCA, not verified. Based on code and docs that may differ from production.

RCA: Nightly order load failed – warehouse (prod)
Confidence: medium · Origin: upstream · Self-healing: yes

TL;DR: The 02:00 UTC load failed because the warehouse API returned errors for 4 minutes. The scheduler
retries at 02:30, so it should fix itself. On-call: check the retry succeeded.

Cause (likely, to be confirmed)
• …

Steps to verify
1. …

Now
• …

Do NOT
• Re-run the full backfill: it duplicates rows.

Permanent fixes
order-loader (owning team)
• …

Also
• The runbook has no section for this alert: add "check the next retry first".

Related
• warehouse API 503 log, 02:10 UTC (link to the original message) — first error, from the logs channel

Rate it: 👍 correct · 🤔 partly right · 👎 wrong
  • Reuse (same ongoing incident as an earlier RCA): "Same as an earlier RCA" with, per earlier RCA, the subjects it covers, a link to it (labelled by its title and time, never a database ID) and its TL;DR. Partly reused RCAs show the same lines under "Already analyzed:".
  • Related lists up to 3 messages from the history (e.g. the error log in another channel that explains an alert) or earlier RCAs, linked to the original messages. The skill cites them by ID and NIMI makes the links, so only real bot messages and real RCAs become links (citations). History, and so citations, is only available when the service runs the skill.
  • Usage limit reached: a one-line notice, no promise of a later RCA.
  • The first line's disclaimer is NIMI_REPLY_DISCLAIMER. Messages stay under NIMI_POST_MAX_CHARS; only the body is shortened if needed, never the header or footer.

docs.title: Where replies go
docs.text:
With NIMI_POST_ENABLED=true, NIMI posts each RCA (and reuse decisions and usage-limit notices) to one or both destinations, chosen with NIMI_POST_TARGET:

NIMI_POST_TARGET Posts go to thread (default) A reply in the alert's own thread, posted as the user whose token NIMI uses. webhook A separate space, through its incoming webhook (NIMI_POST_WEBHOOK). both Both of the above.

docs.title: Posting to a separate space
docs.text:
# nimi-service/.env (or ~/.config/nimi/service.env)
NIMI_POST_ENABLED=true
NIMI_POST_TARGET=webhook
NIMI_POST_WEBHOOK=https://chat.googleapis.com/v1/spaces/<space>/messages?key=<key>&token=<token>

Create the webhook in the destination space (Apps & integrations → Webhooks). The URL contains a secret: it is masked by config, never logged, and errors never include it. run refuses to start if the target includes webhook but the URL is missing or isn't a Google Chat webhook URL.

Webhook posts stay understandable outside the alert's thread:

  • the line under the header links back to the original message: 🔔 Original message in team-alerts: Link;
  • each alert gets its own thread in the destination space: its first post is a new top-level message, and later posts for the same alert (a re-run, a reuse decision, a notice) reply in that thread. Different alerts never share a thread;
  • links to earlier RCAs (in reuse replies) point to the earlier post in the same destination when there is one.

docs.title: Several people, one alert space
docs.text: Each person can run their own NIMI (own database, settings and Claude account) against the same alert space. To avoid duplicate replies in the alert threads, let one instance use thread and the others webhook to their own (e.g. personal) spaces. Each instance triages and runs RCAs independently, so each pays for its own.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: 👍 / 🤔 / 👎 work in both destinations. For webhook posts, NIMI lists the destination space once per reaction interval and fetches reactions only for posts that have (or had) any, so the token's account must be able to read that space (it usually is the user's own space). If it can't, NIMI raises one low-severity red flag and webhook feedback is skipped; posting still works.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• If the destination space is also a registered channel, NIMI ignores its own posts there (by message ID and by their 👁️ NIMI — first line), so it never analyzes its own RCAs.
  • Each destination is tracked separately: if posting to one fails (a red flag is raised), the outbox retries just that one on the next poll, within NIMI_STALE_HOURS.
  • Posts are limited to NIMI_POST_MAX_CHARS, with room kept for the source line.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Run from nimi-service/:

.venv/bin/python -m nimi_service <command> [options]

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Command What it does db upgrade Create or update the schema to the latest migration, then grant the skill reader its views. db revision "<message>" Draft a migration from model changes (review it before applying). db current The database's schema version vs the latest.

docs.title: Channels and ingestion
docs.text: Command What it does gchat-login --client-secret <file> One-time Google login (opens a browser); saves the Chat token to NIMI_GCHAT_TOKEN_FILE. gchat-spaces [--all] Your Google Chat spaces and their IDs (--all: include direct messages). add-channel <provider> <channel> <label> [--rca/--no-rca] [--backfill-days N] [--display-name X] [--notes X] Register a channel, or update a registered one in place (same row; watermark and messages kept). --rca / --no-rca turn RCAs on or off; options you leave out keep their current value (new channels: RCA off, NIMI_BACKFILL_DAYS). The label is always set. channels List registered channels with their watermark. ingest-once Poll all channels once (a channel's first poll backfills; backfill never triggers RCAs). backfill <channel> --days N Pull older history for a channel (label or ID); stored as backfill, no RCAs, watermark untouched; safe to re-run. parse-test [--text "…"] [--channel L] [--kind K] [--sender S] [--limit N] Show how the parser and platform profiles read stored messages (or --text): matched layout, title, signature, and what reparse would change. Writes nothing. reparse Rebuild parses and signatures for all stored messages (after changing parse.py or a profile); moves RCA requests to the new signatures and warns about stale exclusion rules.

docs.title: Running
docs.text: Command What it does run The service loop: ingest, triage, RCA, post, reactions, red-flag retries. status Channels, message counts, request states, an active Claude pause. config Every setting, its effective value (secrets masked) and source.

docs.title: RCAs
docs.text: Command What it does rca <message> [--provider P] [--fresh] [--no-post] Triage and RCA one stored message now (provider message ID). --fresh always makes a new RCA: no reuse and no exclusion rules, and a secret in the message is flagged but doesn't hold it; triage still names the subjects (so later alerts can reuse it per subject) and its "not needed" verdict is overridden. --no-post stores the result but never posts it, not even later through a running service's outbox; read it with show. rca-text "<text>" RCA arbitrary text now (manual request: no triage, nothing posted). show <message\|request_id> [--provider P] [--chat \| --render] [--all] A stored RCA, without a new run: the request (status, triage decision, subjects, skip reason, posts) and the latest result's report. --chat: the chat message as posted (or as it would have been) instead of the report; --render: the chat message rendered now from the stored report, with the current layout and links and no length limit — shows sections that were left out to fit chat, and previews layout changes on past RCAs (not the posted copy); --all: every attempt (incl. errors and timeouts). For a reused request, shows the RCA it reused. release <request_id> Send a request held for critical sensitive data to triage anyway. resume Clear a Claude pause (usage limit, credit, login) now.

docs.title: Exclusion rules
docs.text:
Command What it does exclude add [--like <message>] [--signature K] [--channel L] [--sender S] [--title T] [--status S] [--text X] --reason "…" [--expires 7d] [--yes] Add a rule; previews matching stored messages and asks before saving (--yes skips the question). exclude [list] [--all] Rules with hit counts; --all includes disabled and expired ones. exclude disable <id> / exclude enable <id> Turn a rule off or on.

See Messages that don't need an RCA.

docs.title: Red flags
docs.text: Command What it does red-flags [list] [--all] Open red flags (--all: include resolved and ignored). red-flags resolve <id> [--ignore] [--note "…"] Close a flag as resolved (or ignored).

docs.title: Other scripts
docs.text: Script What it does db/bootstrap.sh Create the database, the service role and the skill reader role on a local Postgres. dev/review_access.sh [grant], dev/review_access.sh revoke Development only: create or remove a read-only role for reviewing stored bot messages and finished RCAs. bin/nimi-sql "<SQL>" Read-only history SQL; run by the skill during service RCAs.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning Channel A registered chat space/channel. Only channels added with --rca get RCAs. Top-level message A message that starts a thread. Only top-level bot messages are analyzed; thread replies are stored as context. Backfill History pulled on a channel's first poll (or with backfill). Never triggers RCAs. Watermark The newest message time seen per channel; the next poll starts there. Signature The parser's coarse "kind of message" key, shared by every occurrence of the same alert (e.g. all "Disk usage high" alerts): volatile parts (numbers, IDs, timestamps, URLs, Kubernetes pod suffixes) removed so repeats of the same alert match, also across pod restarts. Used for history, reuse candidates and exclusion rules. Platform profile A YAML file in nimi-service/parsers/ describing a platform's log layouts, item names to mask, and triage notes. Layout One log line format in a profile; the first layout that matches a message decides its service, logger and title. Subject One affected item a message is about: a table, service, deployment, job, or *. Triage decides reuse per subject. Request One RCA decision for one message (or manual text), with a status. Triage The cheap, tool-less model call that decides reuse / new / not applicable. Reuse Answering a repeat of an ongoing incident with an earlier RCA instead of a new one. Exclusion rule A code rule that skips RCA for matching messages before triage. Stale Older than NIMI_STALE_HOURS when NIMI can process it; gets no RCA. Held A request with a critical secret in it, kept from all models until release. Red flag A recorded problem for an admin: sensitive data, a rule violation or an error. Pause Claude calls stopped because of a usage, credit or login problem. Guard hook The PreToolUse hook that enforces what the skill may do. Project A registered repository the skill may read. Runbook On-call documentation in a project; hints for the skill, never proof. Origin Whether the root cause is internal or upstream. Self-healing Whether a retry at some level re-runs the failed work automatically. Skill reader The read-only Postgres role used by the skill's history SQL.

docs.title: Skill output contract
docs.text: The service reads the skill's text output (rca.py, parse_output). The skill must follow this exactly.

docs.title: Early exits
docs.text:
A single line at the very start of the output, nothing else:

RCA_OUTCOME: not_applicable - <short reason, e.g. "resolved/OK notification">
RCA_OUTCOME: insufficient_context - <what is missing>

docs.title: Full report and chat message
docs.text:
The full report (layout in skills/rca/templates/report.md) is stored in the database. After it comes the chat message, the one message NIMI posts, between two marker lines. The skill writes only its content, as one JSON object with fixed keys (keys and writing rules in skills/rca/templates/chat.md); NIMI owns the layout (chat_message.py):

RCA_CHAT
{
  "title": "Nightly order load failed – warehouse (prod)",
  "context": "`orders` | load job: order-loader, prod",
  "tldr": "2–3 short sentences",
  "cause": {"certainty": "confirmed | likely", "points": ["…"]},
  "verify": [{"where": "… or null", "text": "…", "command": "… or null", "outcomes": ["result → meaning"]}],
  "now": ["…"], "do_not": ["…"],
  "fixes": [{"owner": "…", "items": ["…"]}],
  "also": ["…"],
  "related": [{"ref": "msg:<id> | rca:<id>", "label": "…", "why": "…"}]
}
END_RCA_CHAT
  • title, tldr and cause are required; empty or missing sections are left out of the message.
  • NIMI renders the sections in a fixed order with fixed names (TL;DR inline; Cause, Steps to verify, Now, Do NOT, Permanent fixes, Also, Related as headings with bullets or numbered steps; each step starts with where it runs; commands as code blocks; possible results as sub-bullets under their step). The optional context line goes under the status line. The provider then converts the markup.
  • Markdown headings inside values are removed, and sentences about earlier RCAs are removed everywhere except Related.
  • Values are plain text with `code` and citations only. A single text where a list is expected is treated as a one-item list; unknown keys are ignored.
  • Length: the skill keeps the whole message under ~2,500 characters by editing (summarising, merging, leaving out the least useful items). NIMI never trims text. Only if a message still can't fit NIMI_POST_MAX_CHARS, whole sections are left out (Related, then Also, Permanent fixes, Steps to verify) with a "(shortened; full report stored)" note.
  • Fallback: if the block is missing, isn't valid JSON, or lacks a TL;DR or cause, the post uses the report's title and Summary.
  • Fallbacks, ignored parts and shortening raise one low-severity red flag per request, so a drifting template shows up.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text:
The skill never writes URLs. Inside text values, to point at a stored message (e.g. the error log behind an alert) it writes [label](msg:<message_id>) with the message_id from skill_messages; for an earlier RCA, [label](rca:<result_id>); for code, [label](code:<project key>@<commit>/<path in repo>#L<line>). Before posting, the service checks each one: cited bot messages become links to the original message, cited RCAs link to their post (in the same destination when there is one), and cited code links to the file at that commit on the project's code host, and anything else — unknown IDs or projects, human messages, unsafe paths, Markdown links to URLs — is reduced to its label. Absolute local paths of registered checkouts are rewritten to <project>: <path in repo>. The stored report keeps the citations, so it records which messages each RCA relied on.

The output then ends with this block, as plain lines, one value per line, nothing after it:

RCA_FIELDS
origin: internal | upstream | undetermined
confidence: high | medium | low
self_healing: yes | no | unknown
repo: <project name in the registry, e.g. shop> | none
commit: <short sha analyzed> | none
sensitive_data: none | <where:type, where:type, …>
Field Values origin internal (our code, config, infra, deploy), upstream (source system, third-party API/SDK, data), undetermined. confidence high (direct evidence), medium (strong correlation), low (best hypothesis). self_healing Whether a higher level re-runs the failed work automatically. sensitive_data Types and locations only, never values. where: input, code, config, logs, docs, history. type: e.g. password, api-key, token, webhook-url, private-key, connection-string, email, phone, national-id, customer-data.

A report without the RCA_FIELDS block is treated as incomplete (an error), because it usually means the run was cut short. Invalid values are ignored. Each sensitive_data item raises a red flag.

docs.title: Input context block
docs.text:
The service may prefix the input with a context block; it is the only instruction in the input:

RCA context (from NIMI):
- Analyze only these subjects: <subject>, <subject>
- Already analyzed, do not re-analyze: <subject> (earlier RCA #<id>)
- History SQL: <path>/nimi-sql "<one SQL statement>"
---
<the alert / log text>

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Every setting, its default and meaning. See Configuration for where settings are read from. Secret settings are masked by python -m nimi_service config. <repo> is the NIMI checkout.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning NIMI_DB_HOST 127.0.0.1 Postgres host. NIMI_DB_PORT 5432 Postgres port. NIMI_DB_NAME nimi Database name. NIMI_DB_USER nimi_service The service role. NIMI_DB_PASSWORD unset Service role password (secret). Takes priority over the file. NIMI_DB_PASSWORD_FILE unset File containing only the service password (e.g. a mounted secret). NIMI_DB_SSLMODE unset libpq sslmode, e.g. require. NIMI_DB_SKILL_USER nimi_skill_reader The skill's read-only role (history SQL). NIMI_DB_SKILL_PASSWORD unset Skill reader password (secret). NIMI_DB_SKILL_PASSWORD_FILE unset File containing only the skill reader password.

Without a password or file, libpq falls back to ~/.pgpass, trust or peer authentication. NIMI_DB_DSN is no longer supported.

docs.title: Chat providers
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning NIMI_GCHAT_TOKEN_FILE ~/.config/nimi/gchat-token.json Google Chat user OAuth token (created by gchat-login).

docs.title: Polling and history
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning NIMI_POLL_SECONDS 60 Pause between poll cycles. NIMI_BACKFILL_DAYS 90 Default history pulled on a channel's first poll (add-channel --backfill-days overrides). NIMI_REACTION_DAYS 7 Reactions are re-checked on replies posted within this many days.

docs.title: Triage and RCA
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning NIMI_TRIAGE_MODEL haiku Model for triage. NIMI_REUSE_DAYS 7 Earlier RCAs within this window can be reused. NIMI_ALERT_SENDERS any bot Comma-separated sender IDs (e.g. users/123) allowed to trigger RCAs. NIMI_MAX_PER_DAY 50 Maximum RCA runs per UTC day; further requests are skipped (triage is not capped). NIMI_MAX_PARALLEL 2 Concurrent RCA runs. NIMI_RCA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 900 Timeout of one skill run. NIMI_STALE_HOURS 6 Alerts older than this when NIMI can process them get no RCA. NIMI_SKILL_HISTORY true Give RCA runs read-only history SQL (nimi-sql). NIMI_RCA_PROJECT <repo>/nimi-skill Where the /rca skill lives. NIMI_SYNC_MINUTES 10 How often projects with sync in the registry are updated (only between RCA runs).

docs.title: Claude
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning NIMI_CLAUDE_BIN claude The Claude Code executable. NIMI_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset (~/.claude) Separate Claude login and user config for NIMI. NIMI_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_FILE unset Use an API key from this file instead of the stored login. NIMI_CLAUDE_SETTING_SOURCES user,project Settings layers RCA runs load (subset of user,project,local; empty = none). NIMI_CLAUDE_PASS_ENV unset Extra environment variables passed to Claude, e.g. HTTPS_PROXY,NO_PROXY. NIMI_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MINUTES 15 Pause length after a usage limit when Claude gives no reset time.

docs.title: Replies and notifications
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning NIMI_POST_ENABLED false Post replies to chat (off = dry run). NIMI_POST_TARGET thread Where replies go: thread (in the alert's thread), webhook (a separate space, with a link back to the alert) or both. See Where replies go. NIMI_POST_WEBHOOK unset Incoming webhook URL of the destination space for webhook / both (secret). NIMI_POST_MAX_CHARS 4000 Maximum reply length (the report body is truncated; notes and the feedback line are kept). NIMI_REPLY_DISCLAIMER built-in Disclaimer on the first line of every RCA message (default: "Automated RCA, not verified. Based on code and docs that may differ from production."). NIMI_ADMIN_WEBHOOK unset Incoming webhook of the admin's chat space for red flags (secret). NIMI_GUARD_DENIAL_LOG ~/.local/state/nimi/guard-denials.jsonl Where the guard hook logs denials.

docs.title: Special variables
docs.text: Variable Meaning NIMI_ENV Read exactly this settings file instead of ~/.config/nimi/service.env and nimi-service/.env. NIMI_PYTHON Set by the service for bin/nimi-sql: the Python to run it with.
